title: Asha's Tidy Science Mix-Up
markdown:
The Great Meadow Science Fair arrived with a flutter as big as a bumblebee’s wings. Sunlight sparkled through the oaks. Dew on the grass shone like tiny glass beads. Asha the otter zipped from table to table with a job she took more seriously than breakfast.

Every poster had to sit straight. Every beaker had to sparkle. Every wire had to coil like a sleeping snake.

“Oh dear, oh dear, oh me, oh my,” she muttered, whiskers wiggling, as she nudged a slightly crooked sign for Fizzy Fun with Ferns.

Her tail, usually a smooth rudder, twitched faster than a hummingbird’s wings. Everything had its place. Everything must stay in its place.

Her best friend, Nico the duck, waddled up with a happy quack and a bouncy step. His feathery head bobbed so hard it looked as if he might dance.

“Asha! Asha! Look at my Giggle-Goo-Matic!” he quacked. “It giggles when it’s all done! Listen!”

Nico’s invention was a jumble of colourful tubes, whirring gears, and spinning spoons. It looked more like a playful robot than a science project. He patted a pipe that jiggled.

“It’s a little… wobbly,” he admitted, cheerful as ever.

Just then Dr. Bloom arrived, glasses gleaming like dew after rain. Their kind smile could make even the shyest inventor feel brave. Asha’s tail gave an extra-fast flick-flock.

“Everyone be perfectly still!” she squeaked.

As Dr. Bloom stepped toward Asha’s carefully arranged aisles, a small pile of shimmering glitter tumbled from the Sparkle Science table. It landed with a soft pitter-patter right onto the Wonderful Worms display.

Asha’s whiskers trembled. Her ordered world felt as if it were tumbling with the glitter.

“Oh, no, no, no! This won’t do at all!” she declared, voice rushing. “The worms can’t be next to the sparkle! They’ll get ideas!”

In a whirlwind of fur she began to rearrange everything at surprising speed. She shoved Edible Experiments into the Bouncy Bubbles section. Plant Power was squashed right into Mysterious Magnets. Cloud Creations towered where they did not belong. It was a chaotic mess.

The other inventors looked confused. Pipkin the rabbit blinked his long floppy ears.

“But… my Carrot Clock belongs with the plants,” he said. His invention was a clock made entirely of carrots.

Elgan the badger, who had made a bubbling mud-pie weather predictor, grumbled.

“Now my special mud might get mixed up with Mrs. Hedgehog’s jam! Oh, bother!”

Nico’s Giggle-Goo-Matic was nearly hidden behind the Cloud Creations. Dr. Bloom peered at the jumble Asha had made and sighed, gentle as a blanket.

“Asha, my dear,” they said, “are you quite sure about these new groups? They seem a little… mixed up.”

Then Asha saw her. Millie the field mouse had made a delicate Whispering Wind Chime from tiny shells and dried flowers. Millie’s face was full of sadness. Her chime, meant for gentle music, sat right under the label Roaring Rockets. Millie’s tiny shoulders slumped so much it looked as if she might disappear.

Asha saw it all. Millie’s sad face. Inventors tripping over misplaced projects. The concerned look in Dr. Bloom’s eyes.

Suddenly her worry about perfection felt very small. She remembered how she’d felt when her own inventions hadn’t worked perfectly. This was not only about neatness. It was about friends feeling proud of their hard work. The glitter-covered mix-up sat in her chest like a lump she had put there herself.

“Oh, Millie,” Asha whispered. “I’m so very, very sorry. Your wind chime is the most beautiful thing I’ve ever seen, and it belongs where everyone can hear its whisper. Not near noisy rockets.”

With great care she lifted Millie’s chime and moved it to a sunny spot by the entrance, where the breeze could make it sing. Then, with a deep breath, she helped everyone put their projects back.

She helped Pipkin find his Carrot Clock and tucked it safely next to Root Vegetables R Us. She gave Elgan’s mud-pie a special muddy-protected spot, so no jam would dare get close. She un-squashed Plant Power from the magnets, and she coaxed Edible Experiments away from the bubbles.

Nico’s Giggle-Goo-Matic was given a place of honour in the middle, where everyone could see its cheerful wobbliness. As Dr. Bloom came to judge it, the machine let out a series of bubbly giggles, like tiny champagne corks popping. The happy sound made the meadow laugh.

Dr. Bloom’s eyes twinkled. They looked from the straight posters to the singing chime to Nico’s wobbly honour-spot, and they did not mention aisles at all.

Asha’s tail gave a happy little swish. She had been so worried about everything being perfectly neat that she had forgotten the best part of the science fair: sharing ideas and helping friends. A warm, fizzy sparkle sat in her chest that was not glitter at all.

She did not need every wire coiled like a sleeping snake to feel ready. She needed Millie’s chime in the breeze, Elgan’s mud kept from the jam, and Nico’s giggles where everyone could hear them.
